boardQuestion: Where is policy review drag quietly taxing execution quality before the next board cycle?
bottleneckNarrative: The queue is no longer a local annoyance. It is the main throughput limiter in the lane.
operatingReality: Policy packets still circulate across product, risk, and security after the actual decision is already understood.
riskHeadline: Review queue drag is now the dominant blocker in AI governance execution.
blockingIssue: Too many policy packets still require the same last-mile review group.
headline: AI governance is no longer blocked by proof quality. It is blocked by queue design.
nextMove: Collapse the final approval queue into one board-visible threshold and one owner.

boardQuestion: Which buyer-facing trust lane is losing time because the packet still bounces across owners?
bottleneckNarrative: The handoff chain is the real drag source, not the absence of proof.
operatingReality: Commercial, security, and operations teams still re-open the same packet to add small deltas late.
riskHeadline: Procurement trust is slowed more by handoff churn than by missing evidence.
blockingIssue: No single team owns the full packet from draft through buyer-facing closeout.
headline: Trust throughput is being taxed by packet handoffs, not by missing proof.
nextMove: Assign one buyer-packet owner and retire the duplicate late-stage handoff loop.

boardQuestion: Which release lane still has threshold ambiguity that can reopen work after it looks approved?
bottleneckNarrative: Threshold ambiguity is the main reason the lane reopens late.
operatingReality: Deviation, specimen, and change-control packets still require manual interpretation across teams at the end.
riskHeadline: Closeout ambiguity is still strong enough to reverse apparently-ready work.
blockingIssue: The last-mile release threshold is not bound tightly enough to one owner and one rule.
headline: The lane is being reopened by threshold conflict, not by lack of effort.
nextMove: Bind the closeout threshold to one owner and one exception rule before the next release packet lands.

boardQuestion: Where is one operator carrying too much critical review load in the controls estate?
bottleneckNarrative: The control packet is durable, but the ownership pattern is not.
operatingReality: KYC, merchant review, and treasury signals still converge into one overloaded approval lane.
riskHeadline: One decision owner is now the throughput choke point for too much control work.
blockingIssue: Backup ownership and pre-cleared thresholds are still too thin for this lane.
headline: The lane is waiting on one person too often.
nextMove: Split the final approval burden by control family and publish explicit backup coverage.

bottleneckTheme: Too many systems in one path
boardQuestion: Which platform lane is losing clean execution because too many systems still sit in the same change path?
bottleneckNarrative: The path is not blocked by debate. It is blocked by tool sprawl.
operatingReality: Infra changes, identity updates, and vendor cutovers still fan across too many systems for one clean motion.
riskHeadline: Tool fragmentation is inflating review and rollback complexity.
blockingIssue: The cutover path still crosses too many systems with different owners and rollback semantics.
dependencyMoves: reduce system count in the cutover path
bind rollback to one control plane
headline: Platform execution is carrying too many systems in the same approval path.
nextMove: Split the cutover path into one thinner low-risk lane and one explicit high-risk lane.

boardQuestion: Which stable lane is at risk of quiet delay because evidence freshness is slipping?
bottleneckNarrative: This is a manageable watch lane, not a fire drill.
operatingReality: Outcome proof and donor stewardship stay coherent when cadence stays tight, but drift appears quickly when the schedule slips.
riskHeadline: Freshness drift could quietly reduce board confidence if left unattended.
blockingIssue: Refresh timing is still more manual than it should be.
headline: The lane is stable, but freshness drift is the one weak signal worth watching.
nextMove: Add one lightweight reminder automation before the next stewardship refresh window.
